candidates.locator: Article II — Of the Word, or Son of God, Who Was Made Very Man
candidates.phrase: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God
candidates.rationale: The Article directly names the Son as the eternal, uncreated Word, of one substance with the Father, asserting his eternal filial identity and full divinity.
candidates.chunk_text: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God, of one substance with the Father, took man's nature in the womb of the blessed Virgin; so that two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined together in one person, never to be divided; whereof is one Christ, very God and very Man, who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried, to reconcile his Father to us, and to be a sacrifice, not only for original guilt, but also for actual sins of men.

candidates.phrase: the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father
candidates.rationale: The Confession calls Christ the eternal Word made flesh and the only begotten Son of the Father, asserting his eternal filial identity and divine sonship.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, truly God and truly man, in whom the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united. He is the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father, born of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit. As ministering Servant he lived, suffered and died on the cross. He was buried, rose from the dead and ascended into heaven to be with the Father, from whence he shall return. He is eternal Savior and Mediator, who intercedes for us, and by him all men will be judged.

candidates.phrase: Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God
candidates.rationale: The Article names Jesus Christ the only begotten Son of God and, in the same passage, affirms he is truly God, asserting divine filial identity.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God. He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary, truly God and truly man. He died on the cross and was buried, to be a sacrifice both for original sin and for all human transgressions, and to reconcile us to God. Christ rose bodily from the dead, and ascended into heaven, and there intercedes for us at the Father’s right hand until He returns to judge all humanity at the last day.

sonnet.grammatical_subject: Jesus Christ (named as "the only begotten Son of God")
sonnet.speech_act_note: This is a direct confessional assertion ("We believe...") naming Jesus Christ as Son of God, not a report of an opposing view.
sonnet.floor_reason: Per the family's semantic floor (shared filial identity/relationship), naming Jesus Christ as 'the only begotten Son of God' asserts the required filial identity without needing explicit Nicene 'eternal' language.
sonnet.reason: The title is asserted of the right subject in the standard's own voice, but 'only begotten' sits immediately beside the incarnational clauses (conceived, born of the Virgin Mary), so a reader could conflate the eternal filial relation with the temporal event of the virgin birth rather than reading it as eternal generation.
